warnings: The previous blocking issues have been resolved: the confidence API no longer changes the forward() return signature, preserving compatibility with existing training and analysis scripts.
The confidence value is now correctly documented as an uncalibrated probability proxy rather than a calibrated confidence estimate. This removes the prior methodological misrepresentation.

The confidence computation still relies on explicit temporal averaging of cosine similarity. This remains an explicit modeling assumption that discards temporal information and should be considered when interpreting results.

The temperature parameter is configurable but remains heuristic. Any use of the resulting confidence for thresholding or uncertainty estimation should be validated on held-out LOSO KUL subjects using calibration metrics (e.g., ECE, reliability diagrams, or Brier score).
InfoNCE continues to use pairwise similarity matrices across the batch, consistent with prior validated methodology. No regression was introduced in the contrastive objective.
No evidence of train/test leakage, random subject splitting, or RNG-reset regressions was introduced by this change.
suggested_fixes: If confidence will influence downstream decisions rather than analysis only, add a separate post-training calibration stage instead of interpreting the sigmoid output as a calibrated probability.
Consider returning the raw similarity margin alongside confidence in downstream export scripts to facilitate future calibration and forensic analyses.
Add numerical guards (NaN/Inf assertions or validation checks) around similarity computation for improved robustness during training and inference.
summary: The two previously identified blocking issues have been fully resolved. The MatchNet interface remains backward compatible, the confidence output is no longer incorrectly presented as calibrated, similarity computation has been refactored into a shared implementation without changing the validated InfoNCE methodology, and no new methodological, runtime, or train/test leakage issues were introduced by this diff.
